claim: Regenerative agriculture aims to restore soil health increase biodiversity and sequester carbon through practices like cover cropping and rotational grazing
Vertical farming grows crops in stacked indoor layers using controlled environment agriculture reducing water use by up to 95 percent
Agroforestry integrates trees and shrubs into crop and livestock farming systems improving biodiversity and soil health
The global food system accounts for approximately 26 percent of global greenhouse gas emissions including production transport and waste
Precision agriculture uses GPS sensors and data analytics to optimize crop inputs reducing waste and environmental impact
Food sovereignty is the right of peoples to define their own food systems rather than having them determined by international market forces
Composting converts organic waste into nutrient-rich soil amendment diverting material from landfills and reducing methane emissions
Seed banks preserve genetic diversity of crop species providing insurance against crop failures and resources for breeding new varieties
Aquaponics combines fish farming with hydroponic plant cultivation in a symbiotic system where fish waste fertilizes the plants
Indigenous food systems developed over millennia are often more biodiverse resilient and nutritionally complete than industrial monocultures
